Tomato___Bacterial_spot.name: Bacterial Spot
Tomato___Bacterial_spot.tip: Remove and destroy infected leaves and debris. Use certified disease-free seed, avoid overhead watering, and apply copper-based sprays early. Rotate away from tomatoes/peppers for 2-3 years.

Tomato___Early_blight.name: Early Blight
Tomato___Early_blight.tip: Remove lower infected leaves, mulch to stop soil splash, and space plants for airflow. Apply chlorothalonil or mancozeb on a schedule. Rotate crops and keep plants well-fed.

Tomato___Late_blight.name: Late Blight
Tomato___Late_blight.tip: Acts fast — remove and destroy infected plants immediately. Avoid leaf wetness, apply protectant fungicide (chlorothalonil) before spread, and never compost infected material.

Tomato___Leaf_Mold.name: Leaf Mold
Tomato___Leaf_Mold.tip: Thrives in humidity — improve ventilation, reduce leaf wetness, and lower greenhouse humidity. Prune for airflow, use resistant varieties, and apply fungicide if severe.

Tomato___Septoria_leaf_spot.name: Septoria Leaf Spot
Tomato___Septoria_leaf_spot.tip: Pick off spotted leaves early, mulch to block soil splash, and avoid overhead irrigation. Apply chlorothalonil or copper fungicide and rotate crops each season.

Tomato___Spider_mites Two-spotted_spider.name: Two-Spotted Spider Mite
Tomato___Spider_mites Two-spotted_spider.tip: Spray undersides with water to dislodge mites, then treat with insecticidal soap, horticultural oil, or a miticide. Avoid drought stress and encourage predatory mites.

Tomato___Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.name: Yellow Leaf Curl Virus (TYLCV)
Tomato___Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.tip: No cure once infected — remove affected plants. Control the whitefly vector with insecticides, reflective mulch, and fine netting. Plant TYLCV-resistant varieties.

Tomato___healthy.name: Healthy
Tomato___healthy.tip: No disease signs found. Keep monitoring, maintain good spacing and airflow, water at the base, and feed a balanced fertilizer.
